name: Pamukkale
tagline: White terraces and a Roman spa city
summary: A hillside of white travertine pools with the ruins of Hierapolis on top. One night lets you see it at sunset and again at opening, before the day tours arrive.
seasonNote: Summer midday is blinding and hot on the white rock; winter is cold but the water stays warm and crowds are thin.
arrival: Fly to Denizli (1 hour by shuttle) or take a bus or train to Denizli and a 30-minute minibus to Pamukkale village.
gettingAround: The village and the south gate are on foot. Laodicea and Karahayıt are a short minibus or taxi ride; Aphrodisias needs a car or tour.
cashTip: The village has few ATMs; carry lira for minibuses and small restaurants.
foodTip: Denizli is known for tandır kebabı, slow-roasted lamb eaten with flatbread; village restaurants also do good gözleme.
buyTip: Denizli is Turkey's towel and cotton capital, so buy peştemal towels and bathrobes here.
baseArea: Pamukkale village, within a walk of the lower gate

connections.note: Minibus to Denizli, then train or bus.
From Denizli airport, an hour away.

items.name: Pamukkale travertines
items.summary: A white hillside of calcium terraces and shallow warm pools that you climb barefoot.
items.expect: Shoes off for the whole climb; the surface is ridged and wet, and some pools are dry by rotation.
items.tip: Enter by the lower gate late in the afternoon and walk up for sunset, or be first in at opening.
items.priceNote: Planning estimate per adult in local currency, not a live ticket quote; check current prices and what is included.
items.sourceNote: Editorial selection. Durations, spending allowances and itinerary advice are planning estimates; check opening days and prices with the venue before you go.
whyVisit: A white hillside of calcium terraces and shallow warm pools that you climb barefoot.
There is nothing else like it and it is a UNESCO World Heritage site.
visitFlow: Enter at the lower gate in the village.
Walk barefoot up the terraces to Hierapolis at the top.
items.bestFor: Visitors interested in landscapes and wildlife and big views
tradeoffs: Shoes off for the whole climb; the surface is ridged and wet, and some pools are dry by rotation.
Enter by the lower gate late in the afternoon and walk up for sunset, or be first in at opening.

items.name: Hierapolis
items.summary: A Roman spa city above the terraces with a superb theatre and a vast necropolis.
items.expect: Included in the travertine ticket; the site is spread out with little shade.
items.tip: Walk up to the theatre first, then out along the main street to the necropolis.
items.priceNote: Planning estimate per adult in local currency, not a live ticket quote; check current prices and what is included.

whyVisit: A Roman spa city above the terraces with a superb theatre and a vast necropolis.

visitFlow: From the top of the travertines, climb to the theatre.

items.bestFor: Visitors interested in history and context and architecture and design

items.summary: A warm thermal pool where you swim over fallen Roman columns.
items.expect: An extra fee, lockers and a busy cafe; crowded at midday.
items.tip: Bring a swimsuit and go before 10 am or after 5 pm.

items.name: Aphrodisias
items.summary: A city of sculptors with a 30,000-seat stadium, a monumental gateway and an outstanding museum.
items.expect: About 90 minutes each way by road; very few visitors.
items.tip: Hire a car or join a small tour, and leave an hour for the museum's Sebasteion reliefs.
